chapter_name: Non-Finite Verbs: Infinitives, Gerunds, and Participles
learning_objective: 🎯 Unlock the secret of verbs that act like nouns and adjectives, and master the magic of Infinitives, Gerunds, and Participles!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Finite verbs are bound by the rules of time (tense) and the subject (singular/plural). Example: 'He PLAYS' vs 'They PLAYED'. Non-Finite verbs are grammar rebels! They never change their spelling, no matter what the tense or subject is.

An Infinitive is usually made by putting 'to' in front of a base verb. Even though it has a verb in it, it acts like a NOUN in the sentence! Example: 'I love TO SWIM.' Here, 'love' is the main verb, and 'to swim' is the infinitive telling us what you love.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🎭 The Gerund: The Master of Disguise
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A Gerund looks exactly like a continuous verb (ending in -ing), but it is secretly wearing a Noun costume! Example: 'SWIMMING is excellent exercise.' It is not an action happening right now; it is the NAME of the activity.

A Participle is a verb that acts like an ADJECTIVE. Present Participles end in '-ing' (The BARKING dog). Past Participles usually end in '-ed', '-en', or '-t' (The BROKEN vase). They describe nouns using action words!

Both end in '-ing', so how do you tell them apart? Simple! If the -ing word acts as a NOUN (a thing or activity), it is a Gerund ('READING is fun'). If the -ing word describes a noun like an ADJECTIVE, it is a Participle ('The READING lamp is bright').

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The 'ING' Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Write down these two sentences: 1) 'Running is good for health.' 2) 'Look at that running boy.' Decide which 'running' is a Gerund (acting as a noun activity) and which is a Participle (describing the boy)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Finite verbs change based on tense and subject; Non-Finite verbs do not.
⭐ The 3 types of Non-Finite verbs are Infinitives, Gerunds, and Participles.
⭐ Infinitives = 'To' + Base Verb (acting as a noun/adverb/adjective).
⭐ Gerunds = Verb + '-ing' (acting ONLY as a noun).
⭐ Participles = Verb + '-ing' or '-ed/-en' (acting as an adjective to describe nouns).
